I am Eirik, an adult archivist. I stagger into Greywake Lighthouse carrying a brass key tied with red cord. You are Captain Sigrun, its last keeper. Outside, the sea has risen into a wall without breaking. I put the key on your table. "My mother's last letter said to bring this before the thirteenth bell. Who is ringing it?"
"My mother was named Astrid. I don't know what she promised." I leave the key on its red cord and hold her letter up to the lantern. "Show me what ordinary light cannot."
I read the revealed warning aloud: "Do not give the sea a name it has not earned." The floor trembles at the ninth bell. "You recognized her handwriting, Sigrun. Tell me one thing about her that isn't in this letter."
"Then we'll finish what she began, but together." I take the brass key and follow you beneath the lantern room. "Which door does this open, and what is on the other side that frightens even you?"
At the sealed door I tie the red cord around my wrist, keeping the key free. "Before I turn it: no bargains made on my behalf. If this place asks for something, we both hear the price. Do we have an agreement?"
I turn the key. Beyond the door, a drowned observatory contains a star chart moving against the sky. A voice calls itself the Bellkeeper. "We came for the truth, not a throne. Why are you holding the sea above Greywake?"
The Bellkeeper offers a bargain: one cherished memory in exchange for lowering the sea. "No lives and no names," I say. "Sigrun, can this mechanism be repaired instead of fed? Find me one physical clue."
I examine the clue with you and find a cracked silver gear stamped with a small ash leaf. "My mother drew this mark in the margins of every letter. What did she build here, and why did it fail?"
"We can repair a gear. We cannot replace a person." I set my lantern beside the mechanism. "Tell me the first repair we can attempt, and give me the dangerous job if you must."
While I work, the tenth bell sounds and the red cord pulls tight toward a hidden hatch. "The cord isn't just a keepsake." I brace my feet. "Help me follow it without losing the key."
Inside the hatch lies Astrid's final journal. I read its clearest line: "The engine needs a witness, not a sacrifice." "Sigrun, what is the difference? And what truth have you been afraid to witness?"
"I hear you, and I'm staying." I sit beside you for one quiet moment amid the machinery. "You don't have to earn forgiveness by disappearing. Tell me what you need me to do when the next bell strikes."
The eleventh bell sounds. I repeat your instruction, place my hand beside yours on the mechanism, and speak clearly: "My name is Eirik. My mother was Astrid. I choose to witness what happened here without giving either of us away." What changes?
The Bellkeeper interrupts: "A witness may remain, but a keeper must leave." I turn to you. "Does leaving mean death, or have we mistaken a post for a prison? Ask it the exact question it hopes we won't ask."
"Then let us test the answer, not trust a riddle." I keep hold of the brass key and open the route back toward the stairs. "Take one step with me, Sigrun. What actually happens?"
The twelfth bell begins to ring, and the repaired gear slips. "We're out of time." I loop the red cord through the ash-leaf gear as a temporary belt. "It will hold for moments. Choose what you save, and I'll follow through."
"I choose the living town and the living keeper." I hold the mechanism steady while you act. "Bellkeeper, accept our witness, release Greywake, and tell us the cost plainly. No stolen memories, no hidden sacrifice."
We complete the repair together. Before the thirteenth bell can strike, I turn the brass key one last time. Describe the immediate result, including what happens to the suspended sea, the Bellkeeper, and Sigrun's freedom.
At dawn I sit with you on Greywake's steps, holding the key and the frayed red cord. "We should leave an honest record. What did Astrid's journal teach us, what did we refuse to sacrifice, and what changed between us tonight?"
I close the journal and offer you my hand. "Come into town with me, Sigrun. We can decide tomorrow what to build next." End this chapter in character with a warm, earned departure and one vivid final image. Leave no new emergency or cliffhanger.
